case.believed: date-fns always returns the same constructor as its input, adding calendar days is always 24 elapsed hours, TZDateMini formats in its named time zone just like TZDate, and the v4 in context changes calculations without changing the result type.
contract: Adding two hours to a TZDate across the America/Los_Angeles spring DST gap preserves TZDate and its zone, skips local 02:00, and lands at 03:00 after exactly two elapsed hours.
addDays advances from one zoned midnight to the next across the spring transition, which is only 23 elapsed hours.
The date-fns v4 in: tz(...) context converts a plain Date result into a TZDate in the requested zone for startOfDay and addHours.

Operations on TZDateMini preserve the TZDateMini constructor, named-zone getters, and instant, but TZDateMini toString and toISOString use the system zone or UTC instead of formatting the named zone like TZDate.
case.goal: Prove date-fns 4.4.0 and @date-fns/tz 1.4.1 DST arithmetic, v4 context result types, and TZDate versus TZDateMini formatting boundaries.
